prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: The probe statistics say crit_cross is the strongest (negative) correlate of score and that the baseline product-form cut already gives the lowest crit_cross; the successful C1 gains came from *fewer* cut/wcut nets, so I keep the parent's fan-out-weighted product cut and add a small, rank-based criticality *bonus* that only mildly penalises cutting a net whose pins are all timing-critical (use max-minus-mean of criticality per net, unit-free, scaled small) — this should lower crit_cross without the backbone perturbation that killed c014/c019.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=-0.035 robust(mean-std)=-0.019 min_case=-0.020 seed_std=0.024 tns_mean=-0.008 all_valid=True
  C1: score=-0.002 dWNS=+2.3% dTNS=-1.7% per-seed=[-0.03 -0.00 +0.03]
  C2: score=-0.014 dWNS=-4.7% dTNS=+0.3% per-seed=[+0.00 -0.05 +0.01]
  C3: score=-0.020 dWNS=-2.5% dTNS=-1.1% per-seed=[-0.02 +0.01 -0.05]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->135, wcut 421->419, crit_cross 0.011->0.011, repair_flips 103->103, changed-vs-baseline 0.9%
  C2: cut 318->318, wcut 1007->1003, crit_cross 0.000->0.000, repair_flips 238->239, changed-vs-baseline 2.4%
  C3: cut 582->586, wcut 1955->1978, crit_cross 0.069->0.088, repair_flips 353->353, changed-vs-baseline 1.1%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response:
(1) No. The criticality bonus did not lower crit_cross; C3 worsened (0.069→0.088) and C1/C2 were flat, while total score is negative (-0.035).

(2) C3 moved most: cut 582→586, wcut 1955→1978, crit_cross up, repair_flips unchanged — the bonus perturbed partitioning without reducing critical cross-tier pairs, and slightly increased cut nets. C1/C2 barely changed (0.9–2.4% changed-vs-baseline), consistent with a too-small, rank-based term being swamped by the product cut.

(3) Seed spread (std 0.024, per-seed swings ±0.05) is marginal but not disqualifying; all valid.

(4) Next: gate the bonus on nets with high max-minus-mean criticality only when it also reduces wcut, or drop it and instead directly penalize crit_cross pairs.
